name: Drift Tongue — The Living Slang Atlas
creator: Collaborative neural-feed project seeded by linguist Preethi Okonkwo-Saarinen
description: A self-updating, crowdsourced neural-feed lexicon in which participants submitted neologisms from their local Meridian microcultures — block-level slang, augmentation jargon, synthesis-food terminology, runner cant — tagged with location, tier, and origin story. The atlas became not just a dictionary but a living argument that Meridian spoke dozens of mutually intelligible dialects simultaneously, and that no single 'standard' form was legitimate. Within eighteen months it contained over 400,000 entries and was being cited in academic linguistics papers.
cultural_impact: Drift Tongue became the primary reference for Meridian vernacular across all tiers, used by everyone from the Gray Zone kids to Spire speechwriters trying to sound authentic — which itself generated a wave of mockery and new slang entries documenting the appropriation.
controversy: Axiom Network One attempted to purchase and 'curate' the atlas in 2210, offering to host it on official infrastructure. The resulting community vote to refuse — and the counter-proposal to include the offer itself as a lexicon entry under 'Axiom Reach' — became one of the atlas's most-cited moments.
story_hooks: A new entry has appeared in the atlas that contains embedded steganographic data — someone is using the lexicon as a dead drop.
Preethi Okonkwo-Saarinen's original seed algorithm has a backdoor that no one else knows about, and she's been quietly shaping which entries surface first.
A Tier 1 block's entire local dialect has been systematically deleted from the atlas overnight — someone wants that community's linguistic fingerprint erased.
